3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"net/url"
7		"os"
8		"strings"

11	// ErrInsecureHTTP is returned when the base URL uses HTTP without an explicit opt-in.
12	var ErrInsecureHTTP = errors.New("refusing to use insecure http:// base URL for authentication (use --insecure-http-auth to override)")
13	
14	const (
15		// DefaultBaseURL is the production Entire API origin.
16		DefaultBaseURL = "https://entire.io"
17	
18		// BaseURLEnvVar overrides the Entire API origin for local development.
19		BaseURLEnvVar = "ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL"
20	
21		// AuthBaseURLEnvVar overrides only the auth/login origin (device flow,
22		// auth-tokens management, keyring key). Falls back to BaseURLEnvVar when
23		// unset, which is the right behavior for single-host deployments. Split
24		// hosts (e.g. auth on us.console.partial.to, data on partial.to) set
25		// both.
26		AuthBaseURLEnvVar = "ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL"
27	
28		schemeHTTP  = "http"
29		schemeHTTPS = "https"
30	)
31	
32	// BaseURL returns the effective Entire API base URL.
33	// ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL takes precedence over the production default.
34	func BaseURL() string {
35		if raw := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(BaseURLEnvVar)); raw != "" {
36			return normalizeBaseURL(raw)
37		}
38	
39		return DefaultBaseURL
40	}
41	
42	// AuthBaseURL returns the origin used for the device-flow login, auth-token
43	// management endpoints, and the keyring key under which the bearer token is
44	// stored. ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL takes precedence; otherwise it falls back to
45	// BaseURL() so single-host deployments keep working unchanged.
46	//
47	// The result is canonicalised — lowercased scheme/host, default port stripped,
48	// path/query/fragment dropped, trailing slash collapsed — so the value that
49	// flows into store.SaveToken keys matches what tokenmanager.New emits after
50	// its own NormalizeOriginURL pass. Without this, a user setting
51	// ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://AUTH.example.com:443/ would log in successfully
52	// (saved under the raw form) but every subsequent data-API command would
53	// resolve "not logged in" because the manager probes under the normalised
54	// "https://auth.example.com".
55	func AuthBaseURL() string {
56		raw := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(AuthBaseURLEnvVar))
57		if raw == "" {
58			raw = BaseURL()
59		}
60		return NormalizeOriginURL(raw)
61	}
62	
63	// IsSplitHost reports whether the CLI is configured for split-host —
64	// i.e. ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL points at a different origin than the data
65	// API. Both sides are canonicalised via NormalizeOriginURL before
66	// comparison: AuthBaseURL already does this internally, but BaseURL
67	// only trims whitespace and a trailing slash, so a cosmetically-
68	// different ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL (uppercase host, explicit :443, path
69	// suffix) would otherwise look split when it isn't.
70	func IsSplitHost() bool {
71		return AuthBaseURL() != NormalizeOriginURL(BaseURL())
72	}

81	func ResolveURLFromBase(baseURL, path string) (string, error) {
82		base, err := url.Parse(baseURL)
83		if err != nil {
84			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse base URL: %w", err)
85		}

87		if base.Scheme != schemeHTTP && base.Scheme != schemeHTTPS {

content.text:
Yes — the cleanest fix is: if `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` is set explicitly, auth follows it; only when both are unset do we use the production `us.auth.entire.io` default.

Logic:
```
ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL set    → use it
else ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL set → use that (same-host with the custom data API)
else                         → DefaultAuthBaseURL (us.auth.entire.io)
```

This keeps every scenario ergonomic:
- Production fresh install: split-host (entire.io / us.auth.entire.io) ✓
- Local dev (`ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787`): auth tracks to localhost automatically ✓
- Explicit split: set both, works ✓

The only setup that requires both env vars is "production data API + non-production auth host," which is rare and worth explicit configuration.

Want me to apply this?

message.content: But if we kill the old auth, this is useless, right?

content.text:
Right — you're correct. The "fall back to `BaseURL()`" trick only made sense when a single host could serve both data and auth (v1). If v1 auth is going away, then a localhost data API isn't an auth provider either, so pointing `AuthBaseURL` at it just hands you a URL that 404s on `/oauth/*`. The "smart" fallback would be cargo-culted from the old world.

In a v2-only world, local dev legitimately has two distinct hosts (data backend + auth backend), so setting both env vars is the honest configuration. Current implementation stays.
